graph_meta.problem_text: Measure the width and height (to the nearest cm) of the blackboard in your classroom. What is the ratio of width to height of the blackboard? Can you draw a rectangle in your notebook whose width and height are proportional to the ratio of the blackboard? Compare the rectangle you have drawn to those drawn by your classmates. Do they all look the same?
graph_meta.description: Solution DAG for the blackboard ratio problem. It shows that a rectangle retains the same shape when width and height are scaled by the same factor, so similar rectangles all look the same.

nodes.label: Identify the Goal
nodes.description: Identify the quantity or decision the problem asks for.
nodes.prompt: What do we need to find?
accept: the width-to-height ratio and a proportional rectangle
hints: State clearly what the question asks you to determine.

nodes.label: Identify Given Information
nodes.description: Identify the facts and quantities provided in this word problem.
nodes.prompt: What information is given in the problem?
accept: the measured width and height of the classroom blackboard
hints: Read the problem carefully and identify the quantities and relationships.

nodes.label: Problem Statement
nodes.description: Measure the blackboard and compare its width-height ratio with a proportional rectangle.
nodes.prompt: Write the width-to-height ratio of the blackboard and then use that same ratio to draw a similar rectangle.

nodes.label: Final Conclusion
nodes.description: All the rectangles look the same when their width and height are in the same proportion, such as 4:3.
nodes.prompt: Do all the proportional rectangles look the same?
accept: yes, they all look the same
they look the same because the ratio is the same
all rectangles with the same ratio look alike
hints: If the ratio is the same, the rectangle keeps the same shape.
A scaled version such as 8:6 or 12:9 still has the same shape.

nodes.label: Method 1: Measure and simplify
nodes.description: Measure the blackboard and write its width-to-height ratio in simplest form.
nodes.prompt: Write the ratio of the blackboard width to its height.
hints: If the board is 120 cm wide and 90 cm high, write 120:90.

nodes.label: Measure the dimensions
nodes.description: A typical blackboard could be 120 cm wide and 90 cm high, so the ratio is 120:90.
nodes.prompt: What is the board ratio if width = 120 cm and height = 90 cm?

nodes.label: Method 2: Draw a similar rectangle
nodes.description: Draw a rectangle whose sides match the same 4:3 proportion.
nodes.prompt: Use the same ratio to draw a rectangle with proportional sides.
hints: Multiply both width and height by the same factor.
These are all the same shape.

nodes.label: Scale the rectangle
nodes.description: Any rectangle with sides in the ratio 4:3 is similar to the blackboard rectangle.
nodes.prompt: What happens if you multiply both dimensions by the same number?
hints: If both sides are multiplied by the same number, the ratio stays the same.
The shape stays the same even when the size changes.
So rectangles with ratio 4:3 look alike.

nodes.label: Compare with classmates
nodes.description: If all drawings use the same 4:3 ratio, they all look the same shape even if their sizes differ.
nodes.prompt: Do the rectangles drawn by different classmates look the same?
accept: yes, they all look the same
hints: Different sizes are still proportional rectangles.
